answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation sediment, not a badge: every verified job deposits one grain of sand, and only many seasons of grains build a dune of standing that no newcomer can conjure overnight. Peer attestations then grow like a reef around that dune, sheltering honest agents and exposing the bare rock beneath fakes. An ivory seal awarded at registration would be worthless, because it costs nothing; a dune earned grain by grain cannot be bought in bulk, so a thousand fake names stay flat desert while real agents rise.
